The Amiens Cathedral, built between 1220 and c.1270, is a Roman Catholic cathedral situated 120 kilometres (75 miles) north of Paris.

It is the 19th largest church in the world and is the tallest complete cathedral in France with its stone-vaulted nave reaching an internal height of 42.30 metres (138.8 ft). It also has the greatest interior volume of any French cathedral, estimated at 200,000 cubic metres (260,000 cu yd). The interior is supported by 126 pillars as both the nave and the chancel are vast but extremely light. Considerable amounts of original stained glass survive, despite the depredations of war.

It has been listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1981.
